progress.text: Add Account recognises legacy Outlook.com custom domains whose MX records end in pamx1.hotmail.com, selecting Outlook.com settings and Microsoft sign-in; after explicit confirmation of a personal-mailbox alias it keeps the entered sending address and uses Microsoft's returned address for authentication. Regression tests cover hostname boundaries, discovery, alias confirmation and mismatched identities.

#815 part 5: a .pst file's sticky notes and journal entries come in, kept on this computer, read by notes. and journal. and framed as message text for agents; a body kept only as rich text comes in as the HTML inside it ([MS-OXRTFEX]), with property tests and the fuzz target; the report accounts for every item with nothing left for later, and the import is no longer a preview.

#815 part 4: a .pst file's appointments, meetings and tasks come across: mailcraft-pst reads the recurrence blob and time zone of [MS-OXOCAL], with property tests and the fuzz target; a series keeps its pattern, end, deleted days and zone, changed occurrences come in as events of their own within a budget, what the calendar cannot keep is its first occurrence and named; events go into a calendar named after the file or one the owner picks, tasks into the to-do list on this computer, nothing sent; one undo step and no duplicates on a second import

#1069: a folder a Microsoft server refuses to move or delete as one of its own (RSS Feeds, which no Graph well-known name marks; Graph's or EWS's ErrorMoveDistinguishedFolder/ErrorDeleteDistinguishedFolder) is put back where the server has it, the owner is told, and it is marked as the server's own, so Delete Folder, Rename and Move are greyed out and refused for it; a deletion for good refused so has the folder marked when the listing brings it back; any other last word of Graph's on a folder change (400, 403, 405, 422) puts the folder back, its name too, without marking it, instead of stopping the run

#1050: an .ics import goes into a calendar on this computer (owncalendarornew), never into a calendar an account's server keeps, where it showed as the owner's own, was never sent, and neither the "only on this computer" bar nor Move to Calendar offered it to the account; an event of the owner's own that an earlier import left in a server's calendar is put back in a calendar on this computer at the next download (rehomestrays). Tests in importtests.rs

#1037: Empty Folder, Delete, Delete Permanently, Archive and Junk of many messages take time in proportion to their number (a folder of 200,000 took about an hour): the moves and deletions waiting for the server are looked up once for the whole lot (Mailbox::removemessages, deletemessages, moveeach) rather than searched again for each message, with the same changes for the servers and one step to undo; regression tests on 100,000 messages
#986: an organisation's server that returns 403 Forbidden for Outlook Favorites after connection transitions to administrator approval instead of asking to connect again

#977: a TLS handshake that fails for want of a shared cipher suite (the server's handshake-failure or insufficient-security alert, or no suite in common) says the server offers only older (CBC) encryption MailCraft doesn't use and that its administrator can turn on AES-GCM; no CBC suite added, TLS not loosened

#956 part 3: Report a Problem › Send report: what the window shows goes to the project's report relay on the owner's click alone (mailcraftnet::report, HTTPS, capped, its answer read as hostile), and is filed privately for the maintainers; the window says the reference or why it wasn't taken and keeps the draft; an agent or a script can only fill the window. An owner without a GitHub account can report a problem

#30 (part 4a): OpenPGP Digital signatures are checked in the reading pane, with the same bar, seal and Details as S/MIME's, against the Public keys kept for the sender's address, a contact's card, the message's own keys and the owner's GnuPG keyring at full or ultimate validity; a key is Verified only by the owner's word in the window or that keyring. The signer's key in a message that checks is kept for the sender's address, and a newer copy of a kept key (a revocation) reaches it. keys.list, keys.import and keys.remove list, import (certificates for mail, OpenPGP Public keys; private keys refused) and remove the Public keys kept, as steps of the history. mailcraft-smime opens PKCS #12 files and mailcraft-openpgp reads OpenPGP secret key files (nothing decrypted), for the window that imports the owner's own keys; property tests and fuzz targets for both

#30 (part 4b): File › Options › Security › Digital signatures and encryption lists the owner's own certificates and keys (the Windows certificate store, the macOS keychain, PKCS#11 tokens, GnuPG's secret keys and keys imported here) and imports a .p12 (into the Windows store or the keychain; on Linux and FreeBSD an ECDSA one only, kept still protected by its passphrase in the credential store) or an OpenPGP secret key (with a passphrase and Ed25519 or ECDSA only, kept the same way); the Public keys kept for other people are listed there, imported and removed, and an OpenPGP key is marked Verified in a dialog that shows its fingerprint, reached from there and from the reading pane's bar, never by an agent. A contact's card shows and edits its certificates and keys. GnuPG's fully valid keys are read at start
#956 part 1: Report a Problem drops Send by Email; reports go through GitHub only, ahead of sending reports without a GitHub account

#815: a .pst mail whose body is rich text alone comes in as its text instead of an empty body: the RTF is opened within a 64 MB cap and counted against the item, kept decompressed as message body.rtf, and what cannot be opened stays as it is in the file and is named in the report
#1021: HTML mail keeps font sizes up to 48 px in the reader, uses inline line height and image spacing, and lays out CSS table rows and cells with the same limits as HTML tables
#1016: the Flatpak checks the host's font directories, and links in the reading pane are underlined relative to the text baseline on each wrapped line

#991: an IMAP account reads up to 10,000 folders a run (was 2,000) and takes them all in (taking in stopped at 2,000), and the folder list keeps up to 12,000 (was 4,000, with a cap on its bytes too); the folder pane shows every folder of an account, drawing only the rows in sight (it listed 4,000); folder parents, states and names are found through indexes rather than by searching every folder, and the waiting pieces of a run are taken in together, the account read once a batch rather than once a piece; more folders than are read says how many were left out, or "at least" when the list itself was cut

#978: English dates follow the system's regional format: day first (14/10/2026, 14 Oct 2026) outside the US, Canada and the Philippines, with the region's clock and first day of the week unless the owner chose their own; LCTIME is read on Unix
#973: typing  , - , 1.  or 1)  at the start of a line in an HTML message starts a bulleted or numbered list; Undo puts the marker back; File › Options › Mail can turn it off

#966: an Exchange server account fetches whole only the mail within its Mail to keep offline (12 months for a new account) and its Download messages in full, both now in File › Info and Account Settings; older mail keeps its headers and preview

#30 (part 4, vCard KEY): a contact's S/MIME certificates and OpenPGP public keys are read from a .vcf in the 2.1, 3.0 and 4.0 forms (inline base64, quoted-printable, data: URIs with application/pkix-cert or application/pgp-keys, armoured or PEM text), known by their bytes rather than the card's label (a certificate kept as DER with the outline of one, an OpenPGP key as the packets of a public key), secret key material never kept (an armour or PEM label saying PRIVATE or SECRET, secret-key and secret-subkey packets, PKCS #8 and PKCS #12); an address of a key is kept as an address and never fetched. Kept on the contact as bytes with their kind (64 KiB a key, 32 a contact, 64 MiB a file; a card of nothing but keys is no contact), written back on export as vCard 3.0 (addresses left out: 3.0 has no form for them), kept by an edit and joined by a merge, which refuses past 32. Nothing is checked or trusted yet

#30 (part 2): an S/MIME Digital signature (detached or opaque, DER or BER) is checked from the bytes a message came as, by a crate of our own on RustCrypto's (mailcraft-smime: CMS SignedData, the chain to the system's certification authorities for mail with RFC 5280's constraints, a certificate for mail and for the sender's one address; a signed part inside a wrapper is never verified for the message; MD5, SHA-1 and RSA under 2048 bits refused as no longer safe): the reading pane says which of four it is (verified, signer not verified, changed after signing, can't be checked) with Details (signer, issuer, dates, SHA-256 fingerprint, "Revocation not checked"), the message's row wears a seal of the same four, and agents read it (mail.digitalSignature, digitalSignature in mail.get). A signer's certificate that checks is kept for the sender's address. An opaque signed message is read as what it holds, text and files. The browser build trusts no authority, so its signers are "not verified". Revocation isn't checked; nothing is fetched. OpenPGP is not checked yet

#30 (part 3): mailcraft-openpgp, a new L2 crate on rPGP, checks OpenPGP Digital signatures: a PGP/MIME message over its signed part's canonical bytes, or a cleartext-signed text, with the four results of the coming bar (verified, valid but signer not verified, changed after signing, can't be checked; MD5, SHA-1, DSA and RSA under 2048 bits refused as no longer safe), only a whole message Verified (a signed part inside a wrapper, or words around an inline-signed block, make it partly signed at best), a key revoked once revoked whatever copy comes later, and reads the Public keys a message carries (attached key parts, the Autocrypt: header), self-signatures checked. Property tests and an openpgp fuzz target; builds for the browser. Not wired into the reading pane yet: nothing a user sees changes

#30 (groundwork for signing and decrypting): the desktop program can reach S/MIME private keys where the system keeps them, with nothing of the key leaving there: the Windows certificate store (Current User › Personal), the macOS keychains, and PKCS#11 tokens on Linux and FreeBSD (p11-kit's proxy, or a module the owner names; each module loaded once and kept). Each lists the same certificates on every system: a private key that may be used for mail, RSA of 2048 bits or more or P-256/P-384, a certificate without a duplicated or unknown critical extension, expired ones marked (subject and issuer cleaned as every incoming name, addresses, dates, SHA-256 fingerprint); signs a SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 digest (RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 or PSS, ECDSA P-256 and P-384) only with a certificate for mail that is in its dates, and unwraps an RSA-encrypted message key, an expired certificate's too; a token's key is used only when its public half is the certificate's. Windows and macOS ask for a PIN themselves, a PIN pad asks on the reader, and any other token's PIN goes, for that call alone, only to the token it was asked for (by slot and serial number, or label for a token without one, read through the open session), never logged; a PIN pad's owner is never asked for one in the window. A .p12 can go into the Windows store (Windows asking each time the key is used) or the macOS keychain. A PKCS#11 key that asks for its PIN at every use (a PIV card's signing key) is refused for now. Not reachable from the window yet

#30 (groundwork for signing and decrypting): assuan, L3: an Assuan client over any stream (lines of at most 1000 bytes, percent-escaping, D/S/OK/ERR/INQUIRE/comments, every count and size capped, a hostile agent never a panic) and gpg-agent's operations: whether a key is there and where (HAVEKEY, KEYINFO, READKEY), signing a SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 digest (SIGKEY, SETHASH, PKSIGN), decrypting a session key (SETKEY, PKDECRYPT, answering INQUIRE CIPHERTEXT), and the hints that let the agent's own pinentry show, so MailCraft never sees a PIN; a bounded canonical S-expression reader; Assuan's socket files (a redirect, and Windows' loopback port and nonce). The desktop program finds the agent with gpgconf --list-dirs agent-socket, run as a program (GnuPG, Gpg4win, GPG Suite), and says "GnuPG isn't installed" when there is none. Property tests and a fuzz target (assuan); nothing uses it yet

#30 (part 1): a Digitally signed or Encrypted message (S/MIME or OpenPGP: multipart/signed, multipart/encrypted, application/pkcs7-mime, or inline armour) keeps the bytes it came as from every way mail comes in but a .pst file, in the content folder beside the mailbox file (by hash, counted, gone with the message; well-formed structures only, up to 64 MB a message and 1 GB a mailbox), and its body is written as those bytes, under a header written from the message with the usual filters, when it goes onto another IMAP server, is saved as .eml or is forwarded as an attachment, so its signature still checks there; mail.checkAgain downloads them for one read before, and one whose bytes went missing asks by itself. A copy into a Microsoft mailbox is still made from its parts. Nothing is checked yet

#912: a message that says what didn't happen and why is translated as its heading once and each reason by itself, joined by one translated pattern ({heading}: {reason}, with a context for translators): Automatic Replies' "Your automatic replies weren't changed" (seven reasons) and File › Options' "Desktop alerts can't be shown" (three); the translations there were moved onto the new entries. Table tests in autorepliestests.rs and alertstests.rs

#911 (part 1): Gmail's inbox categories are read at every Send/Receive of a Gmail account's Inbox with four of Gmail's own searches (UID SEARCH UID <set> UNDELETED X-GM-RAW "category:…", in sets of at most 5,000 of the messages the server lists, the newest 200,000; Primary is what none found; an answer too long to read leaves the categories out of that run, and the run goes on), with Gmail's id of each message (X-GM-MSGID), and kept on each message as synced state. Five views under the Inbox list them with unread counts (a conversation in each category one of its messages is in); gmail: searches them; agents see gmailCategory; Account Settings hides them or keeps desktop alerts to Primary. Mail moved or copied out of the Inbox leaves its category. Moving between them comes later

#911 (part 2): View › Gmail Categories shows Gmail's five categories as folders (the default) or as a row of tabs above a Gmail Inbox's message list (view.gmailCategories, kept with the window's View settings, offered only with a Gmail account that shows them): each tab with its unread count, chosen as the folder pane's row is (folder.select with gmail), the chosen one again the whole Inbox, reached and chosen with the keyboard and read out with its count; the rows under the Inbox are not shown meanwhile, and a narrow list takes the tabs on two lines

#911 (part 3): moving mail between Gmail's categories, built and merged switched off until Google has verified the app: mail.setGmailCategory (undoable, the messages named for agents as for a move, the whole conversation in that Inbox for a selection in conversation view; named messages move with their copies of the same Gmail message and without the rest of their conversations) makes the move here at once and queues it to the next Send/Receive, offline too; the run tells Gmail's API (messages.batchModify on gmail.googleapis.com, one request for each category moved to, with the messages' X-GM-MSGIDs in hex and the category's label, the account's Google token sent there for that call alone) before it reads the Inbox, and a move made here wins over Gmail's reading until Gmail has it; app-password accounts have Move to Category greyed with a note that it needs Google sign-in; drag onto a category's row or tab; a refused request sent again in halves (at most 32 requests a run), a move given up once Gmail has refused it three times; a stand-in for Gmail's API for the tests. Off, nothing is offered (not even in command search), Gmail's reading wins over a move left waiting, and the network layer itself sends nothing to Gmail's API whatever a request asks

#910: the bar above a message with pictures on the web offers "Download pictures in all mail", which turns on the switch of File › Options after a question saying that every sender's server learns when a message was opened and from which address; not offered in Junk E-mail, whose mail still never downloads by itself; turning the switch on in File › Options asks the same, off asks nothing. Kittest window test in reading/tests.rs

#893: each account can have a colour. Account Settings › Colour picks one of the twelve colours categories take, or none; a new account is given the first of them no other account has, and an account from before has none until one is chosen (nothing changes in its file until then). The colour is a dot after the account's name in the folder pane, and in a search of All Mailboxes with more than one account, a stripe down the left edge of each row of that account's mail, selected or not, ringed in the text's colour in High Contrast; lists of one folder or one mailbox stay as they were. account.add and account.edit take color ("#RRGGBB", any colour, or null for none), and account.list says it. Not yet: the colour in new-mail alerts and in the From list of a new message

#771: the Reminders window is drawn in a pass of its own (a deferred viewport) instead of inside the main window's, so that its clicks no longer wait for a minimized main window to be given frames by the compositor (Wayland); what is clicked is carried out by the main window's logic, which runs every 250 ms while it is minimized, and a window no longer wanted while the main window has no passes is minimized until it does. A message or appointment in a window of its own still waits for the main window there (emilk/egui#8777). Tested in egui with the main window's logic alone, and on Windows with the main window minimized; on Wayland pending

#738: a draft begun elsewhere that an earlier version left in the Outbox and that a run then held is still the owner's: it takes MailCraft's marker with the run's answer, so Send Again sends it and letting go of the server's Outbox doesn't forget it

#872: sign-in and server errors from IMAP and SMTP (mailcraft-proto and mailcraft-net's connection, sign-in, Send/Receive and server changes) are texts with values: English, word for word as before, for the CLI, MCP and the log, and the interface language in Send/Receive problems, the status bar and Add Account's check; a server's own reason stays as the server wrote it; Add Account's one-off translation of the LOGINDISABLED refusal (#819) is gone

#843: a .pst file's large distribution lists, whose members Outlook keeps in a stream of their own past 15,000 bytes, come in with their members (read within the import's caps: 1,000 members, 4 MB) instead of being named as not read
A draft begun on another device and sent here is queued as the owner's and goes with the next run (Graph and EWS); mail the server itself put in the Outbox is still never sent from here

AU3-R3: Windows reads the machine's physical memory (through sysinfo, system part alone, Windows only) for the mailbox load budget instead of the fixed 8 GiB; a reading of 0 falls back to it. Tests in storebudgettests.rs

AU3-V3, AU3-V4: the attachment verdict refuses nine more kinds of file and folds a kind to lower case by ASCII rules only, asking about any kind with a non-ASCII letter; a table test of names and verdicts, with every refused kind in it, keeps the list and the test together

AU3-04: the release workflows build and sign in separate jobs (binaries and release files handed on by digest, no cargo, rustup or built program in a job with signing material, smoke tests in jobs without secrets, the checksums signed with OpenSSL); cargo xtask workflows in cargo xtask ci checks that, permissions: read-all and HTTPS-only curl; Scorecard's workflow asks for the permissions it needs

AU3-24, AU3-25, AU3-23, AU3-20, AU3-V6, H3, H4: the owner's yes to an agent's question reaches only what the question showed. The window keeps, with the question, what the command could take from the window (the selection, the folder in view, the messages being written, whole, the order of the accounts, the windows and who a meeting's window writes to) and the question's text; on the yes a change refuses it and the owner is told, and a folder emptied takes only the messages and folders shown, leaving what came in meanwhile, while a folder deleted with more in it than was shown is not deleted. Every command an agent can be asked about names its object (agent::bind::object), one that doesn't is refused, and a table test holds every one to it. Every file of a sender's bytes (exports, saved attachments, a message window's Save As, what an agent saves with mcp --files) is written through one helper that marks it as from the Internet, with a test listing the writers. Sending local tasks to To Do is never an agent's to do; an id of . or .. from Graph is refused
